title: Tilt Down
description: A tilt-down rotates the camera vertically from a fixed position, starting higher and ending lower. It can drop from sky or architecture onto a person or object without moving the tripod.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The new fact is below: a body, a key, a grave, a child. Establishing scale above, then landing, keeps rank in the pitch of the head rather than in a descending crane.
It is the wrong tool when you must arrive from a map into a street with true height change. A tilt cannot lower the lens into a crowd; it can only look down at one.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Compose the high start and the low end. Control exposure as you leave the sky.
Keep the support still so the move stays pitch, not boom. Prompt a slow tilt down onto the subject, starting in sky or ceiling and descending to the figure, a measured vertical scan.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it to land on a person or object after establishing scale above. Concrete beat: a ceiling fan, then the sleeper.
Do not use it when the camera itself must come down to eye height.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: A Tilt Up is the opposite pitch. A Crane Down translates through height and can keep walking after the descent.
A Pedestal Down lowers the whole camera with tilt unchanged. Tilt down looks down; it does not sit down.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Citizen Kane uses vertical looking so ceilings and power share a sentence. The Godfather lands from rooms onto faces and objects as rank.
These are pitch grammar, distinct from crane descents that change station.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a Crane Down. The tell is the camera's eyeline dropping through floors, with parallax as objects rise in frame.
The fix: keep the sticks planted, pitch down, end on the lower fact.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Tilt Down in film?
It is a downward pitch of a camera that stays in one position, scanning from a higher composition to a lower one.
Tilt Down vs Crane Down
Crane down physically lowers (and often advances) the camera. Tilt down only rotates, so height of the lens stays put while the look drops.
When should I use Tilt Down?
When the story fact is below the current look and you do not need a new station. Do not use it to enter a street from the sky.
How do I prompt Tilt Down for AI image or video?
Write fixed camera, tilt down from sky or ceiling onto [Subject], no crane, no pedestal. Name the landing object.
